Source: Clanbook: Gangrel, Chapter One ("Stone, Steppe, and Sea"), "The Invicti."

During the late years of Imperial Rome, a Gallic Gangrel Embraced two worshippers of the Syrian sun-god Sol Invictus. One died almost immediately, destroyed by vampire hunters who forced her to face the dawn. The other, a martyred convert who took the name Constanus, styled himself a self-appointed "protector of the undead": he claimed a mandate from the Book of Nod itself that no mortal may raise a hand against one who bears the mark of Caine, and so hunted down mortals who destroyed vampires — regardless of clan, sect, or the vampire's own conduct.

Over the following centuries, Constanus and his brood (who took the name Invicti after their founder's patron cult) parlayed this self-appointed office into a substantial network of debts and boons, becoming the premier political faction within Clan Gangrel and a power to be reckoned with among Kindred more broadly — while making implacable enemies of witch-hunters and vampire-slaying orders in the process.

Storyteller/LARP note: The Invicti as an organized brood ended around 600 AD, when Constanus and his most powerful childer died together in a great fire in northern Italy (at least seven vampires met Final Death); no culprit was ever identified, whether hunters, jealous Kindred, or simple chance. Political fortunes for the survivors collapsed within decades, and by 650 AD the name was largely forgotten. The Invicti make a strong template for a Gangrel-led "vengeance for the fallen" faction or vigilante coterie in any era — a self-appointed avenger sub-plot, a rival Kindred order that considers itself above clan and sect, or a historical antagonist/patron whose fall left behind boons, grudges, and unclaimed influence still worth fighting over in a modern chronicle.

Source: Clanbook: Gangrel, Chapter One, "The Mongol Invasions" and "Storytellers Secret: The Anda."

The Anda (Mongolian for "blood brother") were a bloodline of pure Mongol-blooded Kindred descended, by the clan's own account, from a nameless Methuselah reputed to have burrowed beneath the Gobi Desert since prehistory, after the Cathayans (the vampires of the Far East) drove Gangrel out of Asia. The Anda spent their nights capitalizing on the Mongol conquests, riding with Genghis and Batu Khan's hordes and reconnecting Asian Kindred society with the wider Cainite world as the empire expanded. Some Anda assimilated with Western Kindred who joined the Mongols; others held apart.

The bloodline did not survive the fall of the Mongol dynasty in China: when the Mongol regime there collapsed, the Cathayans rose up and slaughtered every Mongol-aligned Kindred they could find. A handful may have escaped into deep torpor, and more than one elder Gangrel claims (unverifiably) to personally remember Genghis Khan, but as an organized bloodline the Anda are extinct. Childer of the Anda Embraced in the West before the collapse are indistinguishable from ordinary Gangrel and largely do not know any of the bloodline's distinguishing secrets; many of these lines were later destroyed by the Inquisition.

Storyteller/LARP note: Excellent hook for elder or Methuselah-tier antagonists/patrons in a chronicle touching Central Asia, the Gobi, or Kindred history predating the Cathayan expulsion of Western vampires from the Far East. A player character with unexplained Mongol-era memories, an inherited grudge with the Cathayans, or a claim (true or false) of Anda ancestry can be built directly from this material.

Source: Clanbook: Gangrel, Chapter One, "The Nazi Party."

Around the time the fascist Gangrel brood called the Fist rose in western Germany (circa 1938), a separate group calling itself the Waelkyrige emerged in Scandinavia and spread influence through north-central Europe. Its members professed to follow the Viking warrior ethic absolutely and claimed to be modern incarnations of the mythical Valkyries — choosers of the slain — under the leadership of a Gangrel calling herself Brunhilde. If the claim is more than affectation, the group would have made a great many Embraces directly on Second World War battlefields.

Little concrete information about the Waelkyrige survives past the war years; the group is not known to operate in the United States, but rumor holds they remain active in the Black Forest and elsewhere in Scandinavia, deliberately basing themselves in werewolf-contested wilderness — a fact treated by other Gangrel as proof of serious power. Later rumors (a pack of werewolves found frozen and drained in northern Norway in 1977; a Gangrel's disturbing vision of Tyr tearing into Fenris in 1982) are informally linked back to Brunhilde and her circle by Gangrel who track such things, though nothing is confirmed.

Storyteller/LARP note: A ready-made named faction/NPC patron (Brunhilde and the Waelkyrige) for chronicles touching Scandinavia, werewolf-Kindred conflict, or Viking-flavored Gangrel characters and Path of the Feral Heart backstories. Their WWII-era Embraces and their standing feud/detente with local Lupines are open plot hooks left deliberately unresolved by the source material.

Source: Clanbook: Gangrel, Chapter One, "The '90s" (closing roundtable transcript).

The Chronicle of Secrets is a series of prophetic verses concerning the End of Days (Gehenna) in circulation among Kindred by the modern nights. Its authorship and true age are unknown, though those familiar with it argue it predates the Camarilla itself; the sect's justicars and princes officially denounce it (one, Modius, reportedly dismissed it as "spiteful lies to make children out of monsters"), which several Gangrel take as evidence that the elders fear or simply wish to suppress it rather than proof it is false.

Two couplets are singled out by name in the source material:

  • "You will know them by the Wild Ones, who will hunt us even in the strongest city..." — widely assumed by Kindred at large to refer to the Lupines (werewolves), but disputed among some Gangrel, who argue the "Wild Ones" instead describes the clan's own most bestial elders: ancients so overtaken by the Beast that they have become feral, hungry, and monstrous in truth.
  • A passage referencing a coming "Time of Thin Blood" and vampires who can no longer Embrace — read by some as foretelling the rise of the Caitiff and thin-blooded Kindred as a herald of the end.

Storyteller/LARP note: A flexible, deliberately ambiguous Gehenna-prophecy text Storytellers can quote, expand, or contradict as a chronicle-spanning mystery hook. Its Gangrel-specific reading (that the "Wild Ones" are the clan's own frenzy-worn ancients rather than werewolves) gives it particular relevance to Gangrel-heavy chronicles building toward elder or Methuselah-tier threats from within the clan itself.
